A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MGE and Full-Multiscale training work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-restoration experiments, gradient-discrepancy measurements, timing results, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 reports original image-restoration and timing results, retains the appendix experiments, and adds statistical comparisons.

M1.justification: The telescopic gradient estimator, losses, parameter updates, and coarse-to-fine initialization remain unchanged. Removing Algorithm 1's parallel annotation accompanies a clarification of execution, rather than an established change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate denoising, deblurring, inpainting, and super-resolution using STL10, CelebA, and Urban100. The added discussion of attention and possible level choices does not introduce evaluated tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Single-scale training and the same Multiscale, Full-Multiscale, and subsampling variants on the same backbones. The newly cited attention architectures are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported architectures, preprocessing, losses, optimizers, learning rates, iteration schedules, and computational budgets remain unchanged in Tables 7–8 and the workunit appendix. Sequential execution is newly disclosed; the added significance tests concern E5.

E4.justification: Table 2 revises the evidence comparing coarsening with cropping and hybrid subsampling, while retaining the overall coarsening advantage. For example, Full-Multiscale UNet denoising with cropping changes from 0.3497 to 0.2723 MSE. The noise, depth, fixed-budget, and resolution-level analyses otherwise retain their evidence.

E5.justification: Where v3 Table 2 reports mean performance alone, v4 introduces paired t-tests against Single-scale at a 5% significance level throughout the primary coarsening comparisons, with significance annotations. This substantially expands statistical assessment of the central results, without establishing additional training runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises most scores across all four tasks, including ranking reversals. Full-Multiscale ResNet denoising changes from 0.1658 versus Single-scale's 0.1629 to 0.0839 versus 0.0927. Tables 1 and 3–6 retain their values. The PDFs do not explain the numerical revisions.

T1.justification: v4 Appendix A.1 adds a Lipschitz-composition argument extending the O(h) gradient-discrepancy bound to deep CNNs with depth-dependent constants. The existing lemma, hot-start theorem, and coarsening-versus-cropping derivations remain. The main-text assumptions and Equation (12) sketch largely restate existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract's task scope and 4–16× computational-savings claim remain unchanged. The rewritten introduction strengthens the theoretical positioning by claiming rigorous adaptation to non-convex CNN training and assurance against divergence when mixing scales.

C2.justification: v4 clarifies that Figure 2 measures cross-resolution discrepancy rather than full gradient-estimation error and that parallel wall-time gains remain unrealized. It adds substantive discussion of excessive coarsening, attention's locality challenges, and the variance-based interpretation of fixed-budget results.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-access URL, explicitly discloses sequential experimental execution, and recommends a minimum coarsest resolution around 8×8 pixels and batch growth of 2–4× per coarser level. These are documentation and guidance additions; the existing experimental settings remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds Vaswani et al. (2017) and the Swin Transformer citation, removes Shi and Cornish (2021), and more explicitly distinguishes its theoretical contribution from empirical multiscale work. The additional Haber 2017 entry represents the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The introduction's approach and contribution paragraphs are rewritten, and targeted explanatory passages expand the discussion. Broader Impact moves from Appendix A into Section 5, renumbering the appendices. Most existing prose and the principal section sequence remain.

P2.justification: v4 comprehensively adopts the TMLR layout, changing typography, margins, headers, and the author block. Figure 1 becomes a larger standalone display, appendix image grids are cropped and enlarged, and tables are reflowed with statistical annotations added to Table 2. The same figure and table inventory remains.

improvement.justification: Statistical tests, execution clarification, practical guidance, and a code link improve transparency. However, Table 2's unexplained revisions are unreconciled with Table 6's retained four-level denoising scores. Stronger non-convex guarantee claims also lack a corresponding extension of the convex convergence theorem. These benefits and reporting concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
